title: He was executed for refusing to abandon his faith. Every November 24, Sikhs mark the day he chose it anyway. November 24, 2026.
excerpt: Guru Tegh Bahadur's Shaheedi Divas, and the Chennai samosa vendor who built an export business and just won an award named after JRD Tata.
bodyHtml:
He was executed for refusing to abandon his faith. Every November 24, Sikhs mark the day he chose it anyway

Guru Tegh Bahadur, the ninth Sikh Guru, was executed in Delhi in November 1675 on the orders of Mughal emperor Aurangzeb. His martyrdom is commemorated every year on November 24 as Shaheedi Divas - the fixed date set by the Nanakshahi calendar - after he refused to convert and chose execution over abandoning his faith. He is remembered as having died defending the right of others to practice their own faith, not only his own - a sacrifice made on behalf of people outside his own community who were facing the same pressure to convert.

He dropped out of school in 6th grade to sell samosas. Last week, a Union Minister gave him an award named after JRD Tata

J. Haja Funyamin grew up in his family's small samosa business in Pudupet, Chennai. In 2008, he took a loan, bought a freezer, and started Hafa Foods from a rented unit in Red Hills. The company now reports Rs 15.58 crore in turnover, exporting frozen samosas to the UAE, the US, Canada, Singapore, and Sri Lanka. On November 17, 2026, Union Minister Nitin Gadkari named him Entrepreneur of the Year at the JRD Tata Awards.

Two stories today, one thread: a sacrifice made for someone else's freedom, and a business built one freezer at a time until it reached five countries.
